description: This plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and Accuracy for three different metrics, one of which has an obscured label in the legend. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," uses a linear scale ranging from 0.86 to 1.00, with tick marks at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. All three lines include vertical error bars at each data point. The first metric, represented by a solid blue line with circle markers and an obscured legend label, maintains a high, steady trend across the x-axis. It begins at approximately 0.93 at x=0.86, experiences minor dips to roughly 0.96 at x=0.90 and x=0.93, reaches peaks near 1.00 at x=0.97 and x=0.99, and ends at approximately 0.98 at x=1.00. The second metric, labeled "Δ Accuracy," is depicted by a dashed orange line with diamond markers. It starts at approximately 0.29 at x=0.86 and exhibits a general downward trend with fluctuations, declining to about 0.13 at x=0.91, rising to 0.21 at x=0.92, falling to its lowest point of approximately 0.05 at x=0.95, and ending at roughly 0.21 at x=1.00. The third metric, labeled "Initial Accuracy," is shown as a dash-dot green line with square markers. It begins at approximately 0.64 at x=0.86, rises to about 0.84 at x=0.91, dips to 0.77 at x=0.92, climbs to a peak of approximately 0.93 at x=0.95, remains relatively steady before rising again to 0.93 at x=0.99, and finally drops to approximately 0.77 at x=1.00.
